newsitem.title: USA: Congress clears disaster aid, veto threatened.
newsitem.headline: Congress clears disaster aid, veto threatened.

text.p: Congress Thursday approved emergency disaster assistance for more than 30 states, but the bill faces a threatened presidential veto over unrelated issues concerning the census and future government spending.
The Senate approved the $8.6 billion spending bill on a vote of 67-31 and the House approved on a largely party line vote of 220-201.

Republican leaders of both the House and Senate refused to remove two provisions Clinton has said he will not accept -- the first to avert another government shutdown and the second to block the use of sampling in the 2000 census.
The bill provides more than $5 billion in disaster aid for more than 30 states, $1.9 billion to pay for military operations in Bosnia and Iraq and money for other government agencies.

As recently as Wednesday night the president said he would return the bill to Congress swiftly "so they can send me a clean disaster assistance bill immediately that keeps aid flowing to those in need."
The measure fell far short of the two-thirds majority which would be needed to pass the bill over a presidential veto.
